levels.name: The Missing Banner
levels.subtitle: A schoolyard mystery
levels.intro: The welcome banner has disappeared! Meet Maya, follow three golden ribbons, and bring them to the celebration garden.
levels.lesson: Friendship starts with listening and helping everyone feel included.

tasks.title: Ask Maya
tasks.speaker: Maya
lines: Ethan! Our celebration banner is missing. Can you help me find three golden ribbons?
Thanks for helping! Let’s make our celebration fun for all our friends.

choices.label: Let’s look together!
choices.reply: Great! Bounce and explore. Follow the glowing ribbon pieces.

choices.label: Can we skip the party?
choices.reply: We can include everyone! Let’s help prepare an event everyone can enjoy.

levels.name: Cafeteria Clue
levels.subtitle: A delivery we cannot guess about
levels.intro: A replacement delivery arrived without the expected information. Help Chef Marco check the practice plan, prevent cross-contact, and create a non-food activity for every friend.
levels.lesson: Labels can change. A trusted adult should verify ingredients and each student’s individual needs.

tasks.title: Ask Ari
tasks.speaker: Ari
lines: Ari: I want everyone to join our festival, even friends with food allergies. But today’s delivery is different.
Chef Marco is holding it. Help check the information and separate used tools.

choices.label: Ask an adult to help
choices.reply: Exactly! A trusted adult can check labels and each friend’s plan.

choices.label: Guess from the food photo
choices.reply: A picture cannot tell us ingredients or whether something is suitable. Let’s ask an adult.

tasks.title: Lunch tray
tasks.speaker: Cafeteria helper
lines: A tray looks familiar, but ingredients and preparation can change. What should we do before offering it?

choices.label: Have a trusted adult check
choices.reply: Right. We should never guess about food safety.

choices.label: Assume it is the same
choices.reply: Recipes can change. Ask a trusted adult to check before sharing.

tasks.title: Shared utensils
tasks.speaker: Cafeteria helper
lines: Different foods have used these utensils. How can we help avoid cross-contact?

choices.label: Ask an adult to provide clean equipment
choices.reply: Great. Clean equipment and adult guidance help manage cross-contact.

choices.label: Just wipe them with a sleeve
choices.reply: That is not a reliable way to prevent cross-contact. Ask an adult to handle it.

tasks.title: Inclusive lunch activity
tasks.speaker: Ari
lines: What activity could everyone enjoy without needing to share food?

choices.label: Create a table mural
choices.reply: A colorful class mural is something everyone can join!

choices.label: Require everyone to eat the same snack
choices.reply: Friends have different food needs. A non-food activity includes everyone.

levels.name: Label Detectives
levels.subtitle: The allergy evidence trail
levels.intro: Nurse Lina needs evidence: milk, missing details, and a changed soy recipe. Inspect current labels and report them; never taste food to test an allergy.
levels.lesson: A missing warning does not mean a food is suitable. Labels need careful review by a trusted adult.

tasks.title: Meet Maya
tasks.speaker: Maya
lines: Maya: Nurse Lina has three packages from the delivery. Ingredient lists matter, even when the package looks familiar.
Collect evidence. Never taste something to test an allergy; bring food questions to an adult.

choices.label: Find the magnifier!
choices.reply: Great! It’s by the first reading desk.

choices.label: Taste-test to find out
choices.reply: Never taste a food to test an allergy. Let’s use information and adult support.

tasks.title: Package A
tasks.speaker: Label Detective
lines: The ingredient list names an allergen. What should you do before offering it?

choices.label: Do not share it; tell the adult
choices.reply: Good detective work. We should not offer food that may be unsuitable.

choices.label: Remove the visible ingredient
choices.reply: Removing what you can see does not make it safe. Ask an adult.

tasks.title: Package B
tasks.speaker: Label Detective
lines: The label is hard to read and has no visible precautionary warning. Is that enough to know it is suitable?

choices.label: No — ask a trusted adult to verify
choices.reply: Right. No warning is not proof of safety. Adults can check the details.

choices.label: Yes — no warning means safe
choices.reply: A missing warning does not prove the food is safe. Ask an adult.

tasks.title: Package C
tasks.speaker: Label Detective
lines: This brand has changed its recipe. Who should check before anyone eats it?

choices.label: A trusted adult, using the current label
choices.reply: Exactly. The current ingredients matter, even with familiar products.

choices.label: Use last month’s package
choices.reply: Recipes change. An adult should check the current package.

levels.name: Garden Party Prep
levels.subtitle: Allergy-aware activities
levels.intro: Food ingredients can turn up in craft materials and on shared instruments. Check supplies, separate snacks, and make ways to join without eating.
levels.lesson: Inclusive celebrations can focus on art, games, music and friendship rather than shared food.

tasks.title: Meet Leo
tasks.speaker: Leo
lines: Leo: A friend can react to a food ingredient in an activity, too. Let’s check craft supplies and keep snacks away from the instruments as the adult directs.
Everyone can participate without eating.

choices.label: Let’s plan non-food activities
choices.reply: Awesome! Find the craft table, balloon kit, and music box.

choices.label: Only invite friends eating the same food
choices.reply: Friends have different needs. Everyone deserves a chance to join in.

tasks.title: Art table
tasks.speaker: Leo
lines: What could we do at this table instead of using food in crafts?

choices.label: Draw colorful posters
choices.reply: Fantastic! Art supplies can make this a fun food-free activity.

choices.label: Use peanut shells for collage
choices.reply: Food allergens can be risky in activities. Let’s choose non-food art supplies.

tasks.title: Music station
tasks.speaker: Leo
lines: Which activity can include friends who bring different foods or choose not to eat?

choices.label: A group dance and games
choices.reply: Yes! Music and games let everyone join in.

choices.label: A food-eating contest
choices.reply: A food competition may exclude people. Let’s celebrate with music and games.

levels.name: The Big Celebration
levels.subtitle: The festival allergy promise
levels.intro: Listen, prevent food sharing, bring questions to adults, and practice getting immediate help for a possible reaction. Everyone should belong.
levels.lesson: A good ally listens, includes others, and seeks trusted adult help about food-related safety.

tasks.title: Ask Ari
tasks.speaker: Ari
lines: Ari: Our allergy-aware festival is nearly ready. Let’s welcome friends without pressure and practice speaking up if someone feels unwell.
Adults handle food decisions and emergency plans. We can be good allies.

choices.label: Let’s work as a team!
choices.reply: Hooray! Complete the three celebration stations and meet everyone by the banner.

choices.label: Leave someone out?
choices.reply: An ally makes room for everyone. Let’s make the party welcoming.

tasks.title: Welcome station
tasks.speaker: Maya
lines: A friend feels unsure about participating. What should we do?

choices.label: Ask what would help them join
choices.reply: Listening matters. Invite friends without pressuring them.

choices.label: Tell them they must join
choices.reply: Friends have choices. Listen and make them feel welcome.

tasks.title: Game station
tasks.speaker: Leo
lines: Which game gives every friend a way to participate without sharing snacks?

choices.label: Team scavenger hunt
choices.reply: Perfect! Find clues together and celebrate everyone’s ideas.

choices.label: Guess whose food is safe
choices.reply: We never guess about food safety. Choose a fun team activity instead.

tasks.title: Friendship station
tasks.speaker: Ari
lines: A friend asks about a treat. What is a helpful response?

choices.label: Ask a trusted adult to check
choices.reply: That’s being an ally. Never decide for someone else.

choices.label: Say it looks safe
choices.reply: Appearance cannot establish food safety. Get a trusted adult.

chapters: Welcome Street is planning a festival where friends with food allergies can join. The welcome banner is missing; help the crew recover it.
The banner is found. A surprise food delivery puts the allergy plans at risk. Chef Marco needs help.
A delivery we cannot guess about
A replacement delivery arrived without the expected information. Help Chef Marco check the practice plan, prevent cross-contact, and create a non-food activity for every friend.
Chef Marco keeps unverified food on hold. Nurse Lina needs the current labels to investigate three problems.
Nurse Lina needs evidence: milk, missing details, and a changed soy recipe. Inspect current labels and report them; never taste food to test an allergy.
The adults have the evidence. Make sure the festival activities do not create new allergy risks.
Food ingredients can turn up in craft materials and on shared instruments. Check supplies, separate snacks, and make ways to join without eating.
The garden team is ready. Welcome friends without food pressure and practice getting help if someone feels unwell.
Listen, prevent food sharing, bring questions to adults, and practice getting immediate help for a possible reaction. Everyone should belong.
The festival opens with non-food activities and allergy questions with responsible adults. The crew learned to ask, check, prevent cross-contact, include, and speak up.

incident.title: Speak up immediately
incident.event: PRACTICE DRILL — Sam: My throat feels tight after eating.
hazard: A tight throat after eating may be a serious allergic reaction. Get adult help immediately.
context: Adults follow the emergency plan and obtain emergency help.
incident.guided: Practice drill: Sam says his throat feels tight after eating. Call Ms. Rivera now.
incident.adult: I am here. A suspected serious allergic reaction is an emergency. I will follow the emergency plan, give epinephrine promptly as indicated and call emergency services. This was a practice drill.
incident.help: Call the adult now. Do not wait to investigate.
incident.finish: You got adult help immediately. The practice drill is complete.

favor: If someone may be having a reaction, get adult help immediately.
